correctness.rationale: The normalized overlaps of lengths p−r and r give the cross Gram aI+bS, where a=(p−r)/p and b=r/p. Squaring yields the claimed heat multiplier λ=1−4τsin²(θ/2) with spectrum [1−4τ,1]. It is strictly below one almost everywhere but has essential supremum one, so strong convergence and norm one for every power both hold. In an orthonormal pair spanning the range vectors in a nondegenerate fiber, the commutator has off-diagonal entries ±sqrt(λ(1−λ)) up to unitary phase, with eigenvalues ±i sqrt(λ(1−λ)). Outside their full range the continuous matrix multiplier has uniformly bounded inverse; every point in the range admits unit approximate eigenvectors supported in arbitrarily small shrinking frequency neighborhoods, weakly converging to zero, so none is Fredholm there. Positive level sets of sqrt(λ(1−λ)) have measure zero; zeros on the active pair occur only on a null set, leaving p−2 zero directions per frequency. Maximizing on [1−4τ,1] gives the phase transition at τ=1/8, including equality; for r=1 the inequality (p−1)/p²≥1/8 is exactly 2≤p≤6 over the allowed integers. For the moment law, finite support gives a finite vanishing order k, |F(θ)|²~|m_k/k!|²θ^(2k), and λ^(2N)≤exp(−8τNθ²/π²) for |θ|≤π. Parseval and θ=y/sqrt(N) give the Gaussian integral Γ(k+1/2)/(2τ)^(k+1/2), with Parseval factor 1/(2π), including (8πτN)^(-1/4) for an impulse. Independent integer-sum projection checks and exact-rational convolution norms sampled the heat operator and decay constants; the spectral and asymptotic claims rely on analysis, not the finite checks.
residual_risks: The analysis is for the bilateral uniform equal-width problem and the asymptotic is individual for finitely supported data; the finite computations are not an essential-spectrum certificate.

evidence: Theorem 1.4 and eq. (1.2) give a uniform local probability expansion through arbitrary order when the nonmodal-residue sum grows faster than log variance. In the nearest-neighbor lazy walk, the only required modulus is 2, the sum is n·min(2τ,1−2τ)>0 and linear, and the variance is 2τn. The expansion applies at n=2N without degeneracy even at τ=1/4.

The general alternating-projections papers give convergence rates on restricted or dense input classes; the continuous-time lattice heat result gives a rate to the leading mass profile. Those are weaker comparisons for this exact multiplicative constant.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The local Edgeworth theorem covers far more walks and supplies the terms needed for all moment cancellations. The usual first-order local limit theorem alone would not suffice when k>0.

evidence: Using the prior cross-Gram polynomial with the bilateral shift instead of the cyclic shift gives the same continuous Fourier symbols. The finite commutator band function γ sqrt(1−γ²) fills the interval as the frequency sample becomes dense; standard localized packets give Fredholm essentiality, and the nonconstant band has null level sets. Internal atom zero-sum vectors give precisely p−2 extra directions per period. Optimizing the same prior band yields τ≥1/8, and λ^N gives strong but not norm convergence.

For the moment formula let B_d=Σ_(i−j=d)c_i conjugate(c_j). The squared norm is Σ_d B_d p_(2N)(d) for the lazy walk. Binomial expansion gives Σ_d B_d d^j=0 for j<2k and Σ_d B_d d^(2k)=(−1)^k binom(2k,k)|m_k|². Apply the local Edgeworth expansion of order 2k+1 with σ²=4τN. In each higher correction (σ^(-b) times a bounded-coefficient polynomial times the standard Gaussian g evaluated at d/σ, b≥2), the Taylor terms below degree 2k cancel, leaving O(σ^(−b−2k)). The first term σ^(-1)g(d/σ) contributes exactly σ^(−2k−1)g^(2k)(0)(−1)^k |m_k|²/(k!)², with g^(2k)(0)=(−1)^k(2k)!/(sqrt(2π)·2^k k!). Substitution gives the very same Gamma coefficient in the squared norm.

originality.rationale: The two substantive pieces are covered by explicit stronger or equivalent calculations. The older translated-histogram record gives the identical common-refinement Hilbert model on every cyclic period and gives its exact cross-Gram and commutator bands at every sampled frequency. The bilateral symbol, phase, spectral type and kernel dimension follow from that model by Fourier multiplication and the extra null atom directions. The full moment constant, not merely the impulse exponent, is a direct specialization of the bounded-lattice local Edgeworth expansion and the autocorrelation cancellation detailed below. These are mathematical implications of accessible sources, not a verdict based on an inaccessible source or a matching title.
residual_risks: The older finite record is not itself a statement about a bilateral Fredholm spectrum. Its relevance rests on the exact active-cell equivalence and the standard spectral implication, not identity of ambient spaces. The bounded source review does not assign first discovery or exclude still earlier equivalent treatments.

value.rationale: There is expository value in presenting the concrete projections and their diffusion together. As a new scientific finding, however, the band and norm are the known translated-histogram calculation with a bilateral instead of cyclic shift; the moment constants follow from a general local expansion by cancellation of a finite weight. The only extra discrete multiplicity comes from zero-sum vectors inside each atom, a dimensional count. No independently useful, nonmechanical remaining classification was identified that would justify a repair.
residual_risks: This value decision is confined to the frozen classification, not to possible results on irregular meshes, unequal staggered widths, or other evolution operators.
